findings.title: The resume record is single-use in storage but not in memory: a later full-mode host mount in the same JS context resumes again, with no TTL re-check
findings.evidence: onboardingResume.ts keeps a module-level `peekState` and `memo`. clearOnboardingResume() only removes the AsyncStorage key, and NewOnboardingHost's useState initialiser reads peekOnboardingResume() on every mount. Probe P1c, in an isolate: plant a valid record, require the host, mount (step 3), unmount, call clearOnboardingResume(), mount again. Measured: [ADV-P1c] {"first":3,"storageAfterClear":null,"peekAfterClear":{"settled":true,"value":{"step":3,"data":{"language":"ar"}}},"second":3}. Probe P1f mounts the host 2 h after the record was consumed: [ADV-P1f] {"step":3}. Production path: App.tsx:378 mounts the host only while isAuthenticated && needsPreferences. handleLogout (App.tsx:330-335) and account deletion do not reload the bundle. So a user who switched language at step 2 earlier in the session, then logs out or deletes the account and signs up again, starts the new account's onboarding at step 3. Steps 1-2 are skipped and the language from the record is preset; that language already equals the app language. This defeats the stated purpose of ruling A6 and GA7 ("a different account signing in next can never inherit it"; single use) inside one JS context. Data impact is small (the record holds only the language), so minor. [jest] tag=adv-b3a-probes2 start=2026-10-17 13:01:51 end=13:02:10 rc=1: P1c and P1f failed as expected, showing the defect.
findings.fix: Make clearOnboardingResume() also set the in-memory peekState to {settled:true, value:null} and resolve memo to null. Or have the host consume the record once it applies it (for example a consumeOnboardingResume() that nulls the peek). Optionally re-check RESUME_TTL_MS against saved_at at apply time. Add a row: a second host mount after clear or completion renders step 1.

findings.title: GA3 (deletion revoke is never awaited) is not pinned: an awaited revoke survives r47/r47b
findings.evidence: Extra mutant X2 changes `void revokeGoogleAccessBestEffort()` to `await revokeGoogleAccessBestEffort()` in EditProfileScreen. [mut] X2 SURVIVED rc=0 start=2026-10-17 12:58:51 end=12:59:15 restore_sha=OK, against googleButton.b3a and EditProfileScreen.deleteCopy.w314. The r47 mock resolves at once, so awaiting it is invisible. With the real bounded helper, an awaited revoke would hold onAccountDeleted for up to 3 s on a hung SDK. The committed code is correct (fire and forget).
findings.fix: Add an r47 variant with a never-settling revoke mock that asserts onAccountDeleted is still called once, synchronously after clearSession.

findings.title: The ScanCamera denied predicate is under-tested: changing && to || survives R11
findings.evidence: Extra mutant X3 flips && to || in the ScanCameraScreen cameraDenied predicate. [mut] X3 SURVIVED rc=0 start=2026-10-17 12:59:15 end=12:59:39 restore_sha=OK, against cameraDenied.b3a and ScanCameraScreen.permission. R11 exercises only the fully denied object and {granted:false}; Home's R9 matrix (undetermined + canAskAgain:false, denied + canAskAgain:true) is not mirrored for ScanCamera. The committed predicate is correct (the same strict && as Home). Ruling A14 keeps this pad only as cheap defence, so impact is low.
findings.fix: Make R11 iterate R9's four not-denied permission objects and assert scan-camera-permission-cta, not open-settings.

findings.title: logout() awaits the resume clear in its finally, so a hung AsyncStorage.removeItem hangs logout
findings.evidence: Probe P1e makes removeItem never settle for the resume key only: [ADV-P1e] logout with hung resume removeItem -> timeout (2 s race). This is the same class as the pre-existing awaited clearOnboardingDraft() in the same finally, and ruling A6 asked for the clear beside the draft clear. A hung removeItem is not a realistic failure mode.
findings.fix: Optional: `void clearOnboardingResume()`, or bound it like the Google sign-out. Not required by the rulings.

findings.title: Register shows the consent error twice when a social button is pressed without consent
findings.evidence: From source (RegisterScreen.tsx at HEAD): `register-submit-consent-error` renders whenever the shared `consentError` flag is set. A blocked Google or Apple press therefore shows the ConsentRow error at the top and the same message above Create Account. Probe P3c confirms that consent-error appears and that Google and Apple are gated; P4a confirms the submit error is the sibling right before the Create Account button and that the key auth.consent.required exists in both catalogs. The checkbox the message asks for sits at the top of the form; no scrollTo is used, which MR7's "or" alternative allows.
findings.fix: Cosmetic: keep a separate submitConsentError flag set only by the Create Account path.
